in_greek.name: Βιβιάνα
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Βιβιάνα σημαίνει ζωή και ευτυχία
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βιβιάνα προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'βίος' (bios), που σημαίνει 'ζωή'. historical_references.reference: Vibia Perpetua was a young, unmarried Christian woman who, along with her slave Felicitas, was martyred in Carthage, North Africa, during the reign of Emperor Septimius Severus (AD 193-211). Their martyrdom is recorded in the Acts of Perpetua and Felicitas, which is an eyewitness account of their trials and executions. Vibia Perpetua is remembered as a model of Christian fortitude and is one of the earliest known female Christian martyrs.

historical_references.reference: The Basilica of Santa Vibiana in Rome is believed to have been built during the 5th century AD, during the reign of Pope Symmachus (498-514 AD). The church is named in honor of Vibia Sabina, a martyr who, according to tradition, was a daughter of the Roman Emperor Titus and was buried on the site. The Basilica of Santa Vibiana is one of the oldest churches in Rome and is known for its beautiful mosaics and frescoes.
